title: Field note: llms.txt follows the site builder

drafts.text:
I expected an llms.txt file to tell me something about the firm. Mostly it told me the site builder.

Across six samples of small B2B SaaS, agency and professional-services homepages (1,253 sites, 26 Oct to 28 Nov 2026), 32 of 33 Wix homepages had an llms.txt file. On Squarespace it was 3 of 33. Every other platform: 591 of 1,187, about half.

The mechanism is documented. Wix's help center says Wix "automatically generates and maintains" the file and stops updating it once the owner edits it. The three Wix files I read this week follow one template: a heading and a generated summary of the firm. Squarespace appears to need an opt-in. I have not confirmed that in its own documentation.

So on Wix, the description a crawler finds in that file was written by a generator, and the firm may never have read it.

Monday morning: open yourdomain.com/llms.txt and read it. On Wix, correct what is wrong.

Method note: sites found by web search, not random, so likely more SEO-active than average. Homepage and llms.txt, one scan each. Readiness only, not whether any system reads the file.

Confidence: medium.
